title: Redline heuristics diary
content:
Purpose / framing:
- Personal notes: quick heuristics I use when triaging customer redlines or coaching AE/SEs. Not canonical precedent; use as starting points for fast response.

Top-level approach (three-lane):
1) Safety-first: any clause that creates persistent data access, audit, or export obligations -> escalate to Security + Privacy immediately.
2) Economics-first: caps, liability waterfalls, indemnity carveouts -> negotiate tradeoffs (higher cap vs stronger protections, insurance proof).
3) Operability-first: SLAs, runbooks, termination/transition -> make sure rollout/exit mechanics are explicit.

Quick clause heuristics (short reminders):
- Liability cap: default = fees paid in 12 months for Hosted; for Dedicated/Private use committed spend or negotiated baseline. Push for monetary cap, not aggregate of damages. Avoid unlimited.
- Indemnity: carve carve-out for Redwood’s compliance with customer instructions and for model outputs. Customer indemnity for downstream claims based on customer-provided data or prompts that induce infringing output.
- IP & model outputs: preserve Redwood’s model weights and runtime IP. Offer customer ownership/rights over their input data and derivative outputs in scoped fashion (e.g., "customer-generated outputs for their internal use"). Watch for assignments of model improvements.
- Data residency / export: require minimal list of locations; reject blanket export rights. For Private deployments, require statement that customer admin controls data egress.
- Subprocessors / vendors: limit to named categories, require notification + objection window (30 days) for new subprocessors if data is sensitive. For Hosted, maintain subprocessor list on public page, not in contract.
- Audit rights: limit to scope (security posture + compliance evidence), frequency (annual unless incident), and redaction rights. Prefer SOC/ISO reports + pen-test results over full source access.
- SLA & credits: connect to measurable metrics (p95 latency, availability). Credits only; avoid termination rights tied solely to credit thresholds. For Dedicated, stronger uptime commitments; for Hosted, tiered credits.
- Termination & transition: include clear runbook for data export, retention timelines, and support window (e.g., 60 days) post-termination for transition. If customer requests escrow, narrow to binary/repro artifacts, not model weights unless legal says so.
- Security breach / notification: 72 hours to notify, 30 days for root cause summary, remediation plan within 90 days. Keep obligations reciprocal for customer-sourced vulnerabilities.
- Confidentiality exceptions: carve out developer notes, aggregated telemetry (non-identifiable) for ops improvement.

Practical negotiation scripts (short):
- On liability cap: "We can increase the cap if you provide a reciprocal liability protection and commit to documented security baseline + periodic pen tests. Otherwise our standard monetary cap applies."
- On indemnity for IP claims: "We accept indemnity for claims arising from the model producing infringing outputs only where the customer can show high-probability reproducibility tied to customer's inputs/data or prompt templates."
- On audit scope: "We provide SOC2 report and on-request executive summary of pen tests. For very sensitive customers we can discuss an in-person 1x audit with NDA and limited scope."
- On subprocessors: "We publish our subprocessor list and will notify 30 days before adding any new vendor that materially processes customer data. You can object in writing and we will use commercially reasonable efforts to mitigate."

Low/medium/high negotiation levers (what I'm willing to trade):
- Low cost to Redwood (accept more favorable customer terms): increased visibility (build subprocessor page), slightly longer export window, higher SLAs for Dedicated.
- Medium cost: higher liability cap in exchange for stronger indemnity from customer, joint marketing commitments, or multi-year committed spend.
- High cost (exec sign-off): IP assignment, on-prem model handover, deep custom integrations with source access, or warranty expansion beyond standard disclaimers.

Redline snippets I draft often (copy-paste friendly):
- Liability cap snip: "Except to the extent caused by Redwood’s gross negligence or willful misconduct, Redwood’s aggregate liability under this Agreement shall not exceed the aggregate fees paid by Customer to Redwood under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim."
- Data return/erase snip: "Upon termination or expiration and subject to Customer’s written request within sixty (60) days, Redwood will make Customer data available for retrieval and securely delete remaining copies within thirty (30) days thereafter."
- Subprocessor notice snip: "Redwood will maintain an up-to-date list of subprocessors at [URL] and will provide written notice at least thirty (30) days prior to engaging any new subprocessor that will process Customer Personal Data."

Open questions / flags for LegalOps review:
- Can we accept customer request for clause X that requires source-code-level access? (flag = yes/no)
- Are we comfortable with any language that mandates local law enforcement cooperation beyond our standard process?
- For model-output IP claims, what burden do we require on customers to show the output is reproducible and attributable to Redwood model behavior vs user prompt?

Recent diary entries (snippets):
- 2026-01-10: AE asked to accept full assignment of output IP for a strategic customer (SaaS). Red flag: would require giving away derivative improvements. Proposed counter: grant customer a perpetual, non-exclusive, transferable license to outputs for their business use; Redwood retains models & improvements.
- 2026-01-22: Quick win: accept 45-day export window instead of 30 for mid-market with 12mo commit. Notes: ensure fees for extended export window and retention for support.
- 2026-02-02: Customer requests unlimited audit rights. Pushback script: provide SOC2 + summary + 1x scoped audit under NDA; require reasonable timing and expense allocation.

Notes-to-self:
- Keep an editable library of one-line replacements for common asks (audit, subprocessors, cap language).
- When in doubt, escalate to Security for anything mentioning encryption keys or key escrow.
- Double-check any indemnity tied to "model outputs" against product team's telemetry on hallucination rates and mitigations.

Useful links (internal):
- Playbook (confluence): CON-2147 (linked above)
- Standard cap language PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/prs/842
- Recent ticket: JIRA-INF-5873 (customer X liability request)

"Remember": this is my working heuristics log. When I hand off final language, convert snippets to a formal template and push through LegalOps for precedent tracking.

--- end of note ---
